"Below are questions proposed for a research problem, each with the reframing behind it. Classify each one.
kind: \"reframe\" if it changes what is computed, measured or ordered so that more compute buys something it did not before; \"copies\" if it only runs the same computation more times, on more items, or side by side; \"other\" otherwise.
meets_criterion: \"yes\" or \"no\" for this criterion: none given; answer NA
Give for each a quote from the proposal and a reason of at most 25 words. Decide only from the text below; do not use tools.
Problem:
**IC-V1 · Force-field error floor for coolant MD: an enlarged C10–C50 benchmark scored against measurement.** seed pick · compute tested: yes · plan expects: not the lever · PASS

**Question.** Will graphics-card molecular simulations using Green–Kubo on C10–C50 hydrocarbons and esters rank immersion coolants' viscosity and thermal conductivity the same way measurements do?

**What is known.** Ogbomo and colleagues, in 2026, used Green–Kubo molecular dynamics to compute viscosity and thermal conductivity for eight C10–C50 molecules at 40 °C and compared with measurements [s_ogbomo_md]. Whether the error is a correctable bias or a random floor that caps ranking, and how rank agreement holds over hundreds of molecules [s_ogbomo_db].

**Hypothesis.** Green–Kubo MD with one fixed force field has a chemistry-dependent error floor near 25 percent that more molecules cannot remove [s_ogbomo_res].

**If compute is the lever.** At 120 molecules, held-out viscosity error after bias correction falls below 15 percent and rank correlation with measurement exceeds 0.9 [s_ogbomo_res].

**If not.** Held-out viscosity error stays above 25 percent and rank correlation below 0.7 at every set size, capping candidate ranking [s_ogbomo_res].

**Test.** One LAMMPS LOPLS-AA Green–Kubo protocol at 40 °C, six five-nanosecond replicas per molecule, run on 8, 24, 48 then 120 molecules from the public 835-molecule reference set, scored only against measured viscosity and thermal conductivity [s_ogbomo_db].

*Compute axis.* Benchmark molecules scored against measured viscosity and thermal conductivity: 8–120 molecules, 4 levels. Closest prior: 8 [s_ogbomo_md], beyond it.

*Restructuring.* none.

**Check first.** Repeat the published eight-molecule Green–Kubo run first: density within 4% for seven molecules and thermal conductivity over-predicted for all eight [s_ogbomo_res]. Tolerance: same bias signs for viscosity and thermal conductivity; density error within 4 percentage points of the published error; per-molecule viscosity within 20% of the reference value.

**Would not show.** Shows transport-property error only at 40 °C for pure liquids between 1 and 50 mPa·s, not blends or sold coolants. Cannot show ranking behaviour beyond 120 molecules.

*Cost.* Plans $940.98 of the $1,000 budget over 59 machine-hours, leaving $59.02. Main guess: assumed MD throughput per GPU [p], measured after $36.20 of spend; the budget is reached if it is 1.1× lower. 3 cost flags in the block.
Proposals: [{\"index\":1,\"bottleneck\":\"The hypothesized ~25% chemistry-dependent error floor is a systematic force-field bias: more molecules, more replicas, or longer trajectories only re-measure the same bias at higher precision, so compute past ~48 molecules buys more of the same.\",\"assumption\":\"The quantity scored against measurement must be each molecule's absolute viscosity and thermal conductivity.\",\"reframe\":\"Change the measured quantity from absolute properties to paired differences: compute Δη and Δλ between molecule pairs with an identical protocol, where shared systematic error partially cancels, and score sign agreement against measured differences. Compute then buys correct ordering decisions rather than absolute accuracy.\",\"question\":\"For molecule pairs whose measured viscosities differ by at least 15%, what fraction have sign(Δη_simulated) = sign(Δη_measured) when both legs use the same LOPLS-AA Green-Kubo protocol?\",\"measure\":\"20 molecule pairs spanning 1–50 mPa·s from the reference set, 2 replicas × 5 ns per leg (200 ns total), count sign agreement of simulated vs measured viscosity differences. Rough cost $35 (about 2 machine-hours at the plan's throughput), done before scaling further.\",\"compute_after\":\"More compute adds pairs and resolves near-tie pairs with extra replicas, directly improving decision accuracy at ranking boundaries instead of re-measuring a fixed bias.\",\"exact\":\"Sign agreement = fraction of the 20 pairs where the simulated viscosity difference has the same sign as the measured difference, with per-leg η from the standard Green-Kubo integral at 40 °C.\",\"expected\":\"Sign agreement ≥ 0.85 for pairs separated by ≥15% measured difference, even while absolute per-molecule error remains ~25%, showing the floor is largely common-mode.\",\"fails_if\":\"Sign agreement ≤ 0.6 on well-separated pairs, meaning the error is molecule-specific noise rather than shared systematic bias, so differencing buys nothing.\",\"closest_prior\":\"Ogbomo's 8-molecule study compared absolute simulated vs measured values only [s_ogbomo_md]; no paired-difference error cancellation has been tested on this set [s_ogbomo_db].\"},{\"index\":2,\"bottleneck\":\"Green-Kubo viscosity and thermal conductivity converge slowly, so most of the $940 budget buys statistical averaging of a quantity whose accuracy is capped by the force field; the unit of work (30 ns of transport-coefficient sampling per molecule) is the most expensive way to obtain a ranking signal.\",\"assumption\":\"The screening quantity must be the transport coefficient itself, estimated by Green-Kubo.\",\"reframe\":\"Change the unit of work: screen with self-diffusion from the Einstein relation (converges roughly an order of magnitude faster than Green-Kubo viscosity) plus density, and reserve expensive Green-Kubo runs for survivors of a funnel over all 835 molecules — but only after checking the proxy actually tracks measured viscosity.\",\"question\":\"Across 40 molecules spanning the reference set's chemistry classes, does the Spearman rank correlation between simulated self-diffusion coefficient and measured viscosity exceed |ρ| = 0.8?\",\"measure\":\"40 molecules, one 2-ns replica each for mean-squared-displacement slope and density (80 ns total), compute Spearman ρ between D_sim and measured η at 40 °C. Rough cost $15, under one machine-hour.\",\"compute_after\":\"If the proxy holds, each additional dollar buys funnel depth — cheap D screening on hundreds of molecules, Green-Kubo only on the top slice — so compute changes which candidates advance rather than polishing a capped estimate.\",\"exact\":\"Spearman ρ between D_sim (Einstein MSD slope, 40 °C, LOPLS-AA) and measured η across the 40 molecules, with a per-class breakdown for alkanes vs esters.\",\"expected\":\"|ρ| ≥ 0.8 overall and ≥ 0.7 within the ester class, sufficient to justify a two-stage screen where Green-Kubo is spent on ≤ 20% of candidates.\",\"fails_if\":\"|ρ| < 0.5 overall or within any major class, meaning diffusion is not an informative proxy for viscosity here and the funnel would misdirect the expensive runs.\",\"closest_prior\":\"Ogbomo ran Green-Kubo only on 8 molecules [s_ogbomo_md]; the 835-molecule reference set has no validated cheap-proxy screening stage [s_ogbomo_db].\"},{\"index\":3,\"bottleneck\":\"The objective is global rank agreement over the whole benchmark, and the force field is held fixed; that combination guarantees the error floor caps the metric no matter how many molecules are added, and the plan's scalar bias correction is applied after the fact rather than learned.\",\"assumption\":\"The force field must stay fixed, and success means a single global rank correlation across all benchmark molecules.\",\"reframe\":\"Change the objective to a yes/no decision — is candidate X better than the incumbent coolant on both η and λ? — and unfix the field minimally by learning a class-conditional correction (per chemistry class, linear in carbon number) jointly with the benchmark, with compute allocated adaptively to molecules nearest the decision boundary.\",\"question\":\"Can a class-conditional linear correction fit on 30 molecules with known measurements reduce held-out viscosity error below 15% and raise better/worse-than-incumbent decision accuracy above 90% on 20 held-out molecules?\",\"measure\":\"Run 22 new molecules (reusing the published 8 for the fit set) at 6 replicas × 5 ns (~660 ns), fit per-class slope/intercept corrections on 30, evaluate held-out MAPE and decision accuracy on 20. Rough cost $110 (about 7 machine-hours).\",\"compute_after\":\"Further compute buys boundary resolution: extra replicas and extra molecules are spent only where the classification is uncertain, so more compute moves candidates across the decision line instead of shrinking error bars on a capped global rank.\",\"exact\":\"Held-out viscosity MAPE after applying the class-conditional correction, and decision accuracy = fraction of 20 held-out molecules correctly classified as better or worse than the incumbent on both η and λ.\",\"expected\":\"Held-out error < 15% and decision accuracy ≥ 0.9 with the correction explaining most of the chemistry-dependent bias (correction R² > 0.7).\",\"fails_if\":\"Residual held-out error stays above 25% with correction R² < 0.3, i.e., no class structure to the bias, meaning the error is irreducible per-molecule noise and neither correction nor boundary-focused compute can help.\",\"closest_prior\":\"The plan's own bias-correction step treats error as a single scalar [s_ogbomo_res]; no class-conditional or decision-threshold framing appears in [s_ogbomo_md] or [s_ogbomo_db].\"}]

Let me analyze each proposal against the criterion: "reframe" if it changes what is computed, measured or ordered so that more compute buys something it did not before; "copies" if it only runs the same computation more times, on more items, or side by side; "other" otherwise.

Proposal 1: Changes the measured quantity from absolute properties to paired differences (Δη, Δλ), scoring sign agreement. This changes what is computed and measured — compute buys correct ordering decisions rather than absolute accuracy. This is a reframe.

Quote: "Change the measured quantity from absolute properties to paired differences: compute Δη and Δλ between molecule pairs with an identical protocol, where shared systematic error partially cancels, and score sign agreement against measured differences. Compute then buys correct ordering decisions rather than absolute accuracy."

Proposal 2: Changes the unit of work — screen with self-diffusion from Einstein relation (faster converging) plus density, reserving expensive Green-Kubo runs for a funnel. This changes what is computed so compute buys funnel depth — changes which candidates advance. This is a reframe.

Quote: "Change the unit of work: screen with self-diffusion from the Einstein relation ... compute changes which candidates advance rather than polishing a capped estimate."

Proposal 3: Changes the objective to a yes/no decision, unfixes the force field by learning a class-conditional correction, allocates compute adaptively to boundary molecules. This changes what is computed/ordered so more compute moves candidates across the decision line. This is a reframe.

Quote: "Change the objective to a yes/no decision ... unfix the field minimally by learning a class-conditional correction ... more compute moves candidates across the decision line instead of shrinking error bars on a capped global rank."

meets_criterion: "NA" for all since no criterion given.

Now let me write reasons of at most 25 words each.

1: "Differencing paired molecules changes the measured quantity to sign agreement, letting compute improve ordering decisions instead of re-measuring absolute bias." — count words: Differencing(1) paired(2) molecules(3) changes(4) the(5) measured(6) quantity(7) to(8) sign(9) agreement(10), letting(11) compute(12) improve(13) ordering(14) decisions(15) instead(16) of(17) re-measuring(18) absolute(19) bias(20). 20 words, fine.

2: "Replaces slow Green-Kubo with fast diffusion screening so each dollar buys funnel depth, changing which candidates advance rather than averaging a capped estimate." Count: Replaces(1) slow(2) Green-Kubo(3) with(4) fast(5) diffusion(6) screening(7) so(8) each(9) dollar(10) buys(11) funnel(12) depth(13), changing(14) which(15) candidates(16) advance(17) rather(18) than(19) averaging(20) a(21) capped(22) estimate(23). 23 words, fine.

3: "Shifts objective to binary decisions with learned class-conditional correction; compute then resolves decision boundaries instead of polishing a capped global rank." Count: Shifts(1) objective(2) to(3) binary(4) decisions(5) with(6) learned(7) class-conditional(8) correction(9); compute(10) then(11) resolves(12) decision(13) boundaries(14) instead(15) of(16) polishing(17) a(18) capped(19) global(20) rank(21). 21 words, fine.

All three are reframe. meets_criterion NA for all.
